class_id: a documentation edit breaks a generator that parses that document, and the author runs every test suite except the one that would have caught it
feature: any human-written document that a script parses with a strict pattern — a status table, a CHANGELOG, a decision log, a manifest in Markdown — where the format contract lives only inside the parser's regex and the editor is a person writing prose
symptom: the document reads perfectly to a human. A cell that must be exactly `**PARTIAL**` becomes `**PARTIAL - blocked on X**`; a heading gains a clarifying suffix; a row gains a column. Every one of those edits improves the document AS PROSE, which is why they are made and why review waves them through: the reviewer reads meaning, and the meaning is better. The parser then matches fewer rows than it expects. A good parser refuses to emit and fails loudly; a bad one emits a silently short artefact. Either way the break surfaces on the NEXT unrelated PR's gate, minutes to hours later and attributed to whoever opened it, not to the docs change. The deeper trap is which tests the author runs: a documentation change reads as low-risk, so the author runs the suites for the code they were working on and not the one covering the document — and in this repository that test exists, reads the real file, and asserts the exact count.
first_seen: 2026-09-21 — IPODhan. Updating `docs/design/pull-model-completion-state.md` in #872 I wrote two verdict cells as `**PARTIAL - BLOCKED on an owner decision (#854)**` and `**PARTIAL - existing rows only**`, putting a qualifier inside the bold. `scripts/ops/build-plan-board.mjs`'s ITEM_ROW regex requires the third cell to be exactly `**BUILT**` / `**PARTIAL**` / `**NOT BUILT**`, so both rows stopped matching: the parser saw 27 items where it expects 29 and refused to emit, which failed the Detection-Change Gate on every PR opened afterwards — surfacing on #874, an unrelated scheduler fix, and initially read as #874's problem. Two compounding misses of mine. First, before merging #872 I ran the scraper unit suite and the web unit suite and never `scripts/tests/build-plan-board.test.mjs`, which reads the real document and asserts `EXPECT.items === 29` — it would have gone red immediately. Second, when the gate failed I assumed a stale run and rebased twice before reading the log; the log named the cause on its first line.
fix_prs: #874 — the qualifiers move to the FRONT OF THE EVIDENCE CELL, where they read identically to a human and parse cleanly, and both generators re-run (`build-plan-board.mjs` then `render-board.mjs`; running only the first leaves a stale `index.html` that its own detection check catches). The general remedy is not 'be careful with tables': it is that a document under a parser names its format contract IN the document, at the top, in one line a prose editor will read — and that the test covering a file is chosen by WHICH FILE CHANGED, not by which area the author believes they were working in.
detection_check: partially guarded already, and the guard is why this was findable: `build-plan-board.mjs` refuses to emit when the parsed count differs from its expectation, rather than publishing a short table — a loud failure on an unrelated PR beats a quiet 27-item board nobody notices. Unguarded is the pre-merge half. The check worth building is a path-to-suite map: a changed file names the test files that must run before its PR opens, so editing `pull-model-completion-state.md` demands `build-plan-board.test.mjs` the way editing a scraper source demands its tier tests. Without that, 'which suite covers this' is a judgement call made by whoever is most confident the change is trivial.
